seven_q.Q0_posture: Empirical and urgent; the author presents as an independent researcher who discovered a pattern and is compelled to share it, with full awareness of potential bias.
seven_q.Q1_identity: A framework paper arguing that civilizational decay follows a predictable cascade (semantic → familial → institutional → economic) and recovery follows the same sequence via nucleation by small groups.
seven_q.Q2_domain: Interdisciplinary: sociology, history, physics (phase transitions), theology, linguistics.
seven_q.Q3_claim: Civilizational decay is a phase transition with a universal sequence; recovery is possible through nucleation by small, high-coherence groups that restore the semantic layer first.
seven_q.Q4_support: Nine independent metrics converging 1968-1973; cross-civilizational validation (Rome, Weimar, Soviet Union, US); three restoration case studies (Victorian Britain, Second Great Awakening, Meiji Japan); biblical calibration.
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Coherence is measurable and follows physical law; the semantic layer is foundational; nucleation works in supercooled systems.
seven_q.Q6_consequences: If true, recovery efforts must focus on semantic reconstruction by small groups, not legislation or mass movements. If false, the entire framework fails.
seven_q.Q7_kill: If any civilization collapsed economically before semantically, the framework fails. If any civilization restored institutions without prior semantic reconstruction, the recovery model fails.
